messages:
alice_ng: hey all — seeing a recurring latency spike on /v1/stream-gen starting ~11:07 UTC. p95 jumped to ~1.8s (norm ~220ms). looks tied to chunked responses that include tool outputs. any quick ideas? :thinking:

srebot: INC-2025-2146 created — HIGH latency on eng-runtime /v1/stream-gen (auto-alert from latency-slo).

benj_h: grabbing traces now. can you paste a couple request ids?

alice_ng: req ids: req_42a8, req_42a9. pasted minimal logs below:
```
[11:07:12] req=req_42a8 route=/v1/stream-gen seq_len=1204 kernel=matmul_fast status=ok tokens=32 duration_ms=210
[11:07:13] req=req_42a9 route=/v1/stream-gen seq_len=4200 kernel=matmul_fallback status=ok tokens=512 duration_ms=1810
```

dave_runtime: quick summary from profiler: kernel_selector is flipping to fallback matmul_fallback when it sees sequence lengths > 1024 (expected). The fallback is ~6-8x slower for long sequences. But root cause for the spike seems to be combination of two things: (1) streaming requests with intermittent tool-call chunks create long emitted sequences (tool JSON + tracebacks) and (2) batching heuristic is mixing streaming and non-streaming payloads into the same batch which forces longer SLOs and also thrashes the KV cache.

benj_h: got a flamegraph — batching queue shows mixed traffic peaks. KV cache hit-rate for the affected tenant dropped from ~85% -> 12% during the surge. lots of prefix-miss churn.

carol_ops: which tenant is that? is this noisy neighbor or a legit customer workload?

benj_h: tenant=acme-widgets-prod. They triggered tool-calls on nearly every request (external API embed) so responses contain long tool-output blocks. churned our KV prefix namespace because tool-call delimiters change the conversation prefix frequently.

alice_ng: so two failure modes: kernel fallback for long sequences + batching mixing causing both latency amplification and KV pollution. makes sense.

emily_prod: acme-widgets product ops reported real user impact. they've temporarily reduced concurrency on their side but we need infra fixes.

alice_ng: quick mitigation options?

dave_runtime: short term (ASAP):
- disable mixing of streaming + non-streaming requests for the route.
- clamp seq_len estimate used by kernel_selector for streaming so we avoid fallback for typical tool-embedded noise (e.g., cap to 2048)
- reduce max_batch_size for streaming route to 8 to keep latency predictable

patch suggestion (runtime route config):
```yaml
route: /v1/stream-gen
batching:
  allow_mixing: false
  max_batch_size: 8
  latency_target_ms: 200
```

benj_h: agree. also a medium-term fix: normalize KV cache keys to remove ephemeral tool-call markers so the cache doesn't evict entries per tool chunk. currently we include exact tool delim tokens in cache key which is too sensitive.

carol_ops: can we also throttle per-tenant streaming rate at proxy level? acme is high-volume and their tool chain loops every 2-3 requests. put them on a short soft-throttle while we roll fixes.

alice_ng: created small PR with batching config change + kernel clamp. @dave_runtime can you review? PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3145

:dave_runtime: will review now. planning a canary in us-west-2 with 10% traffic.

benj_h: I'll run a KV cache simulation against trace to verify hit-rate improvement after key normalization patch.

carol_ops: I've queued a support ping to Acme, letting them know we're doing a canary and soft-throttling their traffic for 30m. keeping it non-disruptive. :phone:

[~15m later]

dave_runtime: rolled canary config to 10% (us-west-2). early metrics: p95 for streaming route down from 1.8s -> 270ms on canary nodes. KV hit-rate on canary tenant trace improved to ~72%. looks promising.

benj_h: profiler confirms kernel_selector stayed on matmul_fast due to clamp. batching queue no longer mixes streaming with non-streaming on canary.

alice_ng: awesome. schedule to roll to 100% in 30m if metrics stay stable.

srebot: INC-2025-2146 status -> investigating.

[~40m later]

dave_runtime: rolled to 100% traffic. p95 back to baseline across regions. KV hit-rate recovered.

carol_ops: removed soft-throttle on Acme. they confirmed latency improved.

emily_prod: customer follow-up scheduled.

srebot: INC-2025-2146 resolved — latency SLOs restored. root cause: streaming/non-streaming batching mixing + sensitive KV cache keys + kernel fallback on long tool-output sequences.

alice_ng: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) benj to land KV key normalization RFC + bench (2) dave to formalize kernel_selector clamp config (3) product to add guidance for tool-heavy streaming routes in docs. I'll create tickets. :white_check_mark:
